Arithmetic functions

Source: R/operators.R
z3_sum.Rd

  • z3_sum() and z3_prod() add or multiply any number of arithmetic (or same-width bit-vector) expressions; lists are spliced.

  • z3_div(), z3_mod() and z3_rem() are Z3's integer division, modulus and remainder. div and mod follow the SMT-LIB Euclidean convention (0 <= mod(a, b) < abs(b)); rem takes the sign of the divisor as in SMT-LIB. See z3_operators for how this differs from R.

  • z3_abs() is the absolute value: Z3's abs for Int and Real on Z3 4.13.2 and later, and (ite (< x 0) (- x) x) before.

  • z3_to_real() converts Int to Real; z3_to_int() is the floor of a Real; z3_is_int() states that a Real is a whole number.

Usage

z3_sum(...)

z3_prod(...)

z3_div(a, b)

z3_mod(a, b)

z3_rem(a, b)

z3_abs(x)

z3_to_real(x)

z3_to_int(x)

z3_is_int(x)

Arguments

...

Arithmetic expressions or lists of them.

a, b, x

Arithmetic expressions.

Value

A z3_expr.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
v <- z3_ints(ctx, c("a", "b", "c"))
z3_sum(v)
#> <z3_expr Int> (+ a b c)
z3_simplify(z3_mod(z3_int_val(ctx, -7), 2))
#> <z3_expr Int> 1
